title: Stack nudge eligibility guards: humans only, no native stacks
answers: why does the stack nudge not comment on my PR
bot PRs or outside contributor PRs should not get stacked PR nudge
native GitHub stack PR gets stacked PR comment
body:
Invariant: The nudge runs only for PRs whose author is a non-bot with author_association MEMBER, OWNER, or COLLABORATOR, whose body contains the phrase `🥞 Stacked PR`, and which is not already a native GitHub stack (`!github.event.pull_request.stack`).
Enforced at: .github/workflows/stack-nudge.yml:nudge (job-level `if`).
What breaks if skipped: bots or external contributors get an unsolicited comment, and PRs already using native stacks get redundant advice.
Constraints: Keep these as job-level `if` checks so the job never starts; adding a check only inside a step still runs the job and spends a runner.
applies: Any change to the trigger, `if`, or permissions of the Stack Nudge workflow.
says: Automated stack comments should not post on pull requests submitted by external contributors.
Prevent redundant stack advice comments from appearing on pull requests using native stacks.
Bot pull requests receive unwanted automated comments reminding authors about stacked changes.
Why did the stacked pull request helper not comment on my change description?
Stop posting stacked pull request reminders to non-member contributors and automated bots.
search: The stack nudge workflow in .github/workflows/stack-nudge.yml must restrict execution to non-bot pull request authors with MEMBER, OWNER, or COLLABORATOR associations whose PR body contains `🥞 Stacked PR` and is not already a native stack. These eligibility guards are enforced at the job-level `if` in .github/workflows/stack-nudge.yml:nudge to prevent unsolicited comments on bot or external contributor PRs and redundant advice on native GitHub stacks. The conditions must remain as job-level `if` checks rather than step-level checks to ensure the workflow job never starts and avoids wasting a runner.
